Final tax return for a deceased person in Australia (the 'date of death' return)

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 9 Nov 2026

You may need to lodge a final 'date of death' tax return covering 1 July of the income year the person died up to the date of death. The ATO says it's required if the person had tax withheld from their income (including interest or dividends), their taxable income was above the tax-free threshold, or they lodged returns in earlier years or had outstanding returns. Usually the executor or administrator (the legal personal representative) lodges it on the paper tax return for individuals, because myTax and myGov can't be used, or through a tax agent. If no return is needed, send a non-lodgment advice marked 'DECEASED' with the date of death.

Key facts

  • Covers 1 July to the date of death
  • Paper return or tax agent, not myTax or myGov
  • Usually lodged by the executor or administrator
  • Provide for tax owing before distributing the estate

What are the steps?

  1. Notify the ATO of the death and who will manage the estate. Use the online form plus an interview at a participating Australia Post outlet, or the paper form by mail with certified copies of the death certificate, grant of probate or letters of administration, or will. You can lodge the return once you're on the ATO's records as managing the deceased's tax affairs.
  2. Applying for probate or letters of administration? The ATO suggests waiting for the grant before sending the notification, to avoid delays. You can phone the ATO's individuals enquiries line meanwhile to pause the deceased's tax correspondence.
  3. Ask whether any earlier returns are outstanding. The ATO can tell you when you notify it; these must be lodged too.
  4. Check whether a date of death return is needed: tax withheld from income (including interest or dividends), taxable income above the tax-free threshold, or returns lodged in earlier years or outstanding. If none apply, send a non-lodgment advice form with 'DECEASED' and the date of death as the reason.
  5. Gather the information: the person's papers first. As the authorised legal personal representative you can get their tax information and TFN from the ATO; otherwise their former tax agent may help.
  6. Use the paper tax return for individuals (or a tax agent you've appointed, who can lodge online). Write 'DECEASED ESTATE' at the top of the first page, give the name as 'LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE OF [name] (DECEASED)', mark 'No' to lodging future returns, and sign 'on behalf of' the deceased.
  7. Include income and deductions up to the date of death, plus the cost of preparing the return (such as tax agent fees) even though it's incurred after the death. Income the estate receives after the death goes in a separate trust tax return.
  8. Provide for any tax owing before distributing the estate. The ATO says the executor or administrator may otherwise be personally liable.

Frequently asked questions

Do you have to do a tax return for a deceased person in Australia?

Often, yes. The ATO says a date of death return is required if, in the income year they died, the person had tax withheld from income (including interest or dividends), had taxable income above the tax-free threshold, or had lodged returns in earlier years or had outstanding ones. If none apply, send a non-lodgment advice instead.

Who lodges a deceased person's final tax return?

Usually the authorised legal personal representative, meaning the executor or administrator. You must first notify the ATO of the death and be entered on its records as the person managing the deceased's tax affairs. If someone else lodges, the ATO assesses the return and decides what action to take.

Can I lodge a deceased person's tax return on myTax or myGov?

No. The ATO says myTax and myGov can only be used by the account holder for their own return, so a date of death return uses the paper tax return for individuals, even to claim a franking credit refund. A tax agent appointed by the executor or administrator can lodge online.

What period does the final tax return cover?

From 1 July of the income year the person died up to the date of death. In the ATO's example, someone who died on 4 March 2026 has a return covering 1 July 2025 to 4 March 2026.

Who receives a tax refund for a deceased person?

The ATO releases any refund or franking credits to the authorised legal personal representative. If there isn't one, it decides whether it can release them, taking into account the will or, if there's no will, the rules of succession.

What happens to a HELP debt when someone dies?

Study and training loan repayments are assessed automatically. If income in the final return is above the minimum repayment threshold, the assessment includes a final repayment; after that, any remaining debt is cancelled.
